title: Underived total tensor comparison through the canonical affine chart
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and $P^\bullet,N^\bullet$ arbitrary unbounded cochain complexes of $A$-modules. Write $C$ for termwise associated sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] followed by termwise restriction along $X.\operatorname{toSpec}\Gamma$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. There is an isomorphism of cochain complexes $\operatorname{Tot}(C(P^\bullet)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X} C(N^\bullet))\cong C(\operatorname{Tot}(P^\bullet\otimes_A N^\bullet))$, with total tensor as in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. No K-flatness or derived localization occurs.

proof.text: Extract the uniquely determined affine tilde tensor morphism from affine_tilde_tensor. Its pure-global-tensor formula determines it uniquely by tensor-product extensionality and the tilde/global-sections adjunction. Applying that formula to module maps proves naturality in each factor; NatIso.ofComponents assembles these isomorphisms into tildeTensorNatIso.

Transport the existing strong monoidal structure on scheme-module pullback along restrictFunctorIsoPullback for the canonical affine chart. Functor.Monoidal.transport gives the restriction functor U a natural invertible tensor comparison; its oplax tensorator is packaged as Functor.OplaxMonoidal.δNatTrans U. This bypasses the separately stated sectionwise restriction comparison, since only existence of a total-complex isomorphism is required.

The tilde functor S and the restriction functor U are left adjoints, hence preserve all small coproducts. Binary biproduct preservation makes each additive. Apply HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctorComparison first to tildeTensorNatIso and then to δNatTrans U. The recorded total-bifunctor comparison theorem makes both chain maps invertible, including for arbitrary unbounded input complexes. Invert the U comparison and compose it with the image under U.mapHomologicalComplex of the inverse S comparison. The resulting isomorphism has exactly the stated source and target.
